71:Tec2,function solve(task, deadline) {
  const n = task.n, r = task.r, W = n >>> 5; // 448 bits -> 14 words
  const K = r >>> 5;                          // 224 bits -> 7 words
  // Build rows: M[k] has bit i = bit k of column i
  const M = [];
  for (let k = 0; k < r; k++) M.push(new Uint32Array(W));
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const hex = task.h[i];
    for (let b = 0; b < r / 8; b++) {
      const byte = parseInt(hex.substr(2 * b, 2), 16);
      for (let bit = 0; bit < 8; bit++) {
        if ((byte >> bit) & 1) {
          const k = b * 8 + bit;
          M[k][i >>> 5] |= (1 << (i & 31));
        }
      }
    }
  }
  const pop = (v) => {
    v = v - ((v >>> 1) & 0x55555555);
    v = (v & 0x33333333) + ((v >>> 2) & 0x33333333);
    return (((v + (v >>> 4)) & 0x0F0F0F0F) * 0x01010101) >>> 24;
  };
  const getBit = (row, i) => (row[i >>> 5] >>> (i & 31)) & 1;

  let bestW = Infinity, bestSet = null;
  const TARGET = 79;

  const buildSet = (e, xorVec, pivotCol) => {
    // e: array of free columns; xorVec: Uint32Array(K) bits over rows
    const set = e.slice();
    for (let k = 0; k < r; k++) {
      if ((xorVec[k >>> 5] >>> (k & 31)) & 1) set.push(pivotCol[k]);
    }
    return set;
  };

  while (Date.now() < deadline - 500 && bestW > TARGET) {
    // Copy matrix
    const A = M.map(row => Uint32Array.from(row));
    // random column order for pivot search
    const order = new Array(n);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) order[i] = i;
    for (let i = n - 1; i > 0; i--) {
      const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
      const t = order[i]; order[i] = order[j]; order[j] = t;
    }
    const pivotCol = new Array(r);
    const isPivot = new Uint8Array(n);
    let used = 0;
    for (const c of order) {
      if (used === r) break;
      const w = c >>> 5, m = 1 << (c & 31);
      let p = -1;
      for (let k = used; k < r; k++) if (A[k][w] & m) { p = k; break; }
      if (p < 0) continue;
      const tmp = A[p]; A[p] = A[used]; A[used] = tmp;
      for (let k = 0; k < r; k++) {
        if (k !== used && (A[k][w] & m)) {
          const rk = A[k], ru = A[used];
          for (let q = 0; q < W; q++) rk[q] ^= ru[q];
        }
      }
      pivotCol[used] = c; isPivot[c] = 1; used++;
    }
    if (used < r) continue;

    // Free columns and their syndrome-like vectors V_j (bits over pivot rows)
    const free = [];
    for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) if (!isPivot[j]) free.push(j);
    const F = free.length;
    const V = new Uint32Array(F * K);
    for (let f = 0; f < F; f++) {
      const j = free[f];
      for (let k = 0; k < r; k++) {
        if (getBit(A[k], j)) V[f * K + (k >>> 5)] |= (1 << (k & 31));
      }
    }
    const popV = new Int32Array(F);
    for (let f = 0; f < F; f++) {
      let s = 0;
      for (let q = 0; q < K; q++) s += pop(V[f * K + q]);
      popV[f] = s;
      if (1 + s < bestW) {
        bestW = 1 + s;
        bestSet = buildSet([free[f]], V.subarray(f * K, f * K + K), pivotCol);
        if (bestW <= TARGET) break;
      }
    }
    if (bestW <= TARGET) break;

    // Lee-Brickell p=2
    const tmp = new Uint32Array(K);
    outer:
    for (let a = 0; a < F; a++) {
      const ao = a * K;
      for (let b = a + 1; b < F; b++) {
        const bo = b * K;
        let s = 0;
        for (let q = 0; q < K; q++) {
          s += pop(V[ao + q] ^ V[bo + q]);
        }
        const w = 2 + s;
        if (w < bestW) {
          for (let q = 0; q < K; q++) tmp[q] = V[ao + q] ^ V[bo + q];
          bestW = w;
          bestSet = buildSet([free[a], free[b]], tmp, pivotCol);
          if (bestW <= TARGET) break outer;
        }
      }
    }
  }

  // Compose answer, sorted positions
  if (!bestSet) return [];
  const out = Array.from(new Set(bestSet)).sort((x, y) => x - y);
  return out;
}

6f:["$","details",null,{"className":"spoiler","children":[["$","summary",null,{"children":"Task text, as every rig got it"}],["$","pre",null,{"className":"term scroll","style":{"maxHeight":240},"children":"Syndrome decoding (codeword), a random [448, 224] binary code.\nH is 224 by 448 over GF(2). \"h\" lists its 448 columns, each 224 bits as 28 hex bytes: bit i of the column is bit (i % 8) of byte floor(i / 8). \"s\" uses the same layout.\nFind a nonzero c in GF(2)^448 with H c = 0. Score: the weight of c (number of ones).\nLower is better. For scale: one Gaussian elimination gives weight about 112.\nTo close the block: score <= 79.\nAnswer: a JSON array of the positions (0-based) where the vector is 1."}]]}]
